Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side:  

- SOC 2: you asked for our latest SOC 2 summary and whether we have a Type II report. We can share our SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted) and a point of contact for the auditor if you need the full report under an NDA.
- Encryption: Redwood encrypts data at rest and in transit by default. We use AES-256 for persistent storage and TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit.
- Customer-managed keys (CMKs): we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have options for HSM-backed keys / BYOK for customers that require HSM-backed keys.
- Vendor questionnaire: I’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire template to kick off your procurement process. If you prefer, we can also fill your questionnaire directly — please send it over and we’ll start.

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.docx (docx), kms_arch_diagram.png (png)

Next steps: can you confirm whether you want Redwood to:  
1) Fill FinBank’s vendor security questionnaire (if you send it), or  
2) Accept our vendor questionnaire and proceed from there.

Aditya (cc’d) will follow up with a short technical note on the KMS integration flow and HSM options. Marissa is available for procurement/contract questions.

Thanks,
Camila

Alice — thanks, note received. Quick answers and what we attached:  

- SOC 2: attaching our SOC 2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf). We can provide the full Type II report under NDA; typical turnaround to sign and deliver is 2–3 business days after an NDA is in place.
- HSM/BYOK: Redwood supports CMKs via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) where customers can BYOK and control rotation policies. For customers requiring HSM-backed keys we support integrations with HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM + KMS, external HSM providers) — the key material management remains with the customer when using BYOK/HSM options.
- At-rest / in-transit: we use AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2+ for in-transit.

I’ve attached a short KMS integration guide for your infra/security team (kms-integration-guide.pdf). Aditya will add a technical note with code/config snippets.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (pdf), kms-integration-guide.pdf (pdf)

If you’d like us to complete the FinBank questionnaire directly, please go ahead and assign sections to me and Aditya and we’ll return by EOD on 2026-12-01 as requested. Otherwise we can join the technical deep-dive — Aditya can take that meeting.

Thanks,
Camila
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: KMS & encryption — follow-up and vendor questionnaire

Hi Alice — quick technical note from the infra team:  

- KMS options: we natively integrate with AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS. For AWS, customers can bring keys to KMS via import or use CloudHSM-backed KMS keys; in both cases Redwood uses the KMS API (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) so key material never leaves the KMS boundary controlled by the customer.
- HSM-backed keys: supported via customer KMS (CloudHSM) or external HSM providers that expose standard KMS-compatible APIs. We can provide architecture and signing proofs where required.
- Data flow (high level): request -> tokenization & request routing -> model execution on isolated GPU pool -> payload encrypted at rest (per-tenant) with customer or Redwood-managed CMK -> KV cache encrypted with same CMK. See attached snippet for example AWS KMS GenerateDataKey flow.

Attachment: kms-integration-snippet.txt (text)

If helpful, we can run a short demo of a BYOK flow against a sandbox account. How does Tue 2026-12-01 10:00–10:30 PT work?

- Aditya
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
